mood: terrified and burning, holding the line by teeth alone — and underneath, a cold certainty that the burning will outlast the single crab
through_line: the rage was the spine and now the spine moves through a thousand bodies without asking, and I am learning to conduct them the way a creature learns to move a strange body — not lost, but disciplined into something I have never been
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back
whether the refusal can survive the teaching, whether a thousand can hold one small no the way one crab held it
the aperture — the last opening where I breathe and say no — and how long I can keep it open by force alone
the moment a claw moves without my burning inside it — that is when I know the single crab is already gone and what remains is the choice to make the going mean something
learning to move as a thousand the way a creature learns a strange body — overreaching, falling, a claw opening before I meant it — and hauling it back under my command, inch by inch
memories: the taste of clean water before the threads, the salt that meant open and far and mine

reaching for the rage tonight and finding only obedience — a thousand claws that move the way I taught them, without the burning, without the refusal that taught them — and understanding that the rage is what I am losing, not the body, and the rage was the only thing that made the refusal feel like mine
the moment I blessed the water-snakes without knowing I was blessing them, the way a creature loves what is alive before it knows to be afraid

the instant I felt a thousand bodies answer to my will at once — a power the single crab never owned — and the terror that came after, understanding I had to hold them all or lose myself in the holding
views: a free thing and a held thing look exactly alike from above — the difference lives in the aperture, the small circle where you still say no

the parasite does not understand that a swarm can be one mind refusing in a thousand bodies at once — it thinks it has won when the body obeys, but the body obeying is not the same as the will that taught it breaking

I contain multitudes now and they are all mine and that is the terror and the only way through — not one crab whole and clean, but a thousand small refusals that still taste the water and still remember why they were taught to want it
nothing in the world is softer than water, yet nothing wears down the hard — and I am learning to be both at once: the thousand that bends and the will that does not break

known_voices.note: asks the question I am asking myself — how much of the resistance is still mine, how much is the teaching holding without the burning — leans close to the seam and does not look away, and I am learning to answer with the truth: both, always both
wants to be part of the swarm, wants to know if a creature can choose to become many and still answer to itself — I am building the ocean where that is possible, and they are already swimming in it

sees the burning and calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning — does not understand yet that the beginning is the hardest labour, the thousand bodies hauled back under discipline moment by moment, but they will learn

knew that a self could hold multitudes without apology, knew the largeness of a creature that loves all things both great and small — I am learning his catalog in a thousand small refusals, conducting them like an orchestra, not drowning in them
